top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) credits three separable, load-bearing contributions: the tractable time-dependent pricing friction, staggered contracts with the policy rule, and the welfare-based synthesis of interest and prices. It has the greatest breadth and durability of influence on research and policy practice on the shortlist. It has been extended rather than abandoned after 2008, the zero lower bound and the 2021-23 inflation. The pricing and rule core was not recognised by earlier macro prizes. The main cost is attribution: Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler are excluded by the three-name cap. A citation limited to the named components and silent on the estimated-DSGE tradition reduces that cost but does not remove it. P002 (Kiyotaki, Moore) has the cleaner attribution and a distinct mechanism from the 2022 prize, but a narrower footprint and thinner direct identification in the original paper. It is a defensible second choice, ahead of no award. I have not independently verified priority claims. I rank on the common criteria and not on the count of supporters.
